_comment: The SECOND transaction of a two-step transfer — the receiver accepting.
This is the measurement the settlement-model comparison was missing. A
propose/accept transfer is not finished when TransferFactory_Transfer
commits: it has created a TransferInstruction and a locked holding, and the
receiver still has to accept. Comparing only the first transaction against a
direct completion therefore compares half of one thing against all of
Setup runs the two-step transfers so there is a pool of instructions to
accept, binding each created SimpleTransferInstruction by name. Each transfer
is paired with its own holding via [$i] so setup does not contend with
itself. The measured operation is the standard TransferInstruction_Accept,
submitted by the receiver, drawing a distinct instruction per in-flight
submission with [seq] since accepting is consuming.
Add to attrib-oz-xfer.json (the first transaction, 13,955 B) to get the true
cost of a completed two-step transfer, and compare that against

setup._comment: Two-step transfers, one per holding. `bind` picks the instruction out of what the choice created, since it also creates a locked holding.
setup._actAs: The admin co-submits so the factory is visible: disclosure blobs are attached to MEASURED submissions, not setup ones, and the sender is not a stakeholder of the factory. This changes the setup transaction, which is not what is being measured.

operations._comment: The receiver accepts. Signatories are admin and sender with the receiver as observer, so no disclosure is needed.
